items.title: Sleep and Memory
items.text: Many teenagers believe that staying up all night is the best way to prepare for an important exam. [1] In fact, researchers have found that the brain uses sleep to store what it has learned during the day. [2] Because of it, students who sleep well after studying usually remember more facts than those who stay awake until morning. [3] The effect is especially strong for difficult material, such as new vocabulary or math formulas. [4] A sensible routine, therefore, is to finish studying at a reasonable hour and protect at least eight hours of rest. Even a short nap after class can give the brain a small chance to organize new information. Parents and teachers can help by encouraging regular bedtimes during exam weeks instead of praising students who study until dawn.

qs.q:
Where does the following sentence best fit in the passage?
"This storing process is known as memory consolidation, and it mostly takes place during deep sleep."
qs.why: ‘This storing process’는 두 번째 문장의 ‘store what it has learned’를 가리키고, 다음 문장의 ‘Because of it’이 이 설명을 받아요. 그래서 [2]가 알맞아요.

qs.q: What does "The effect" in the fourth sentence refer to?
o: Students feeling tired after studying all night long
Students finding new vocabulary easier to spell aloud
Students remembering more after a good night's sleep
Students scoring higher because they study for longer
qs.why: ‘The effect’는 바로 앞 문장의 ‘잠을 잘 잔 학생이 더 많이 기억한다’는 결과를 가리켜요.

qs.q: In the fifth sentence, "sensible" is closest in meaning to
o: reasonable
fashionable
dangerous
temporary
qs.why: ‘sensible routine’은 합리적인 습관이라는 뜻이라 reasonable과 가장 가까워요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: How students can find more time for late-night study
Which school subjects are hardest for teenagers to learn
Why important exams should begin later in the morning
Why good sleep helps students keep what they study
qs.why: 글 전체가 수면이 학습한 내용을 저장하는 데 도움을 준다는 내용이에요.

items.title: Cities on Two Wheels
items.text: Many large cities are trying to reduce traffic by encouraging people to cycle to work. [1] To ease that fear, some cities have built separate bike lanes so that riders no longer share the road with cars. [2] Others offer rental bikes that can be picked up at one station and returned at another. [3] After these changes, the number of daily cyclists in several cities nearly doubled within three years. [4] Local shops also noticed that cyclists stopped more often and tended to buy small items several times a week. As a result, many business owners who once opposed bike lanes now support them. City planners add that wider lanes, bright lighting and secure parking would help even more people feel comfortable choosing a bicycle.

qs.q: According to the passage, how do the rental bikes work?
o: Riders must return them to the same station within an hour.
Riders can take one at a station and leave it at another.
Riders pay a monthly fee to keep a bike at their homes.
Riders borrow them only from local shops along the road.
qs.why: 세 번째 문장에서 한 정거장에서 빌려 다른 곳에 반납할 수 있다고 해요.

qs.q:
Where does the following sentence best fit in the passage?
"However, many people hesitated at first because they were afraid of cycling beside fast cars."
qs.why: 다음 문장의 ‘that fear’가 가리키는 두려움이 [1]에 들어갈 문장에 나와야 하고, ‘However’는 첫 문장의 권장 내용과 대조돼요.

qs.q: Why did many shop owners change their attitude toward bike lanes?
o: Bike lanes made the roads easier for delivery trucks.
Cyclists came into their shops more often than before.
The city paid them for supporting the new lanes.
Cyclists bought larger items than drivers usually did.
qs.why: 자전거 이용자가 더 자주 가게에 들러 물건을 샀기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What does "these changes" in the fourth sentence refer to?
o: the stricter traffic rules for drivers
the higher prices at local shops
the fear of riding next to fast cars
the new bike lanes and rental stations
qs.why: 앞에서 설명한 자전거 도로와 대여 서비스를 가리켜요.

items.title: Why Bees Matter
items.text: Honeybees are small, but they play a very large part in the food we eat every day. [1] As they fly from flower to flower looking for sweet nectar, they carry pollen on their legs and bodies. [2] Without it, many crops such as apples, almonds and blueberries would produce far smaller harvests. [3] Unfortunately, bee populations have dropped in recent years because of disease, lost habitats and chemicals used on farms. [4] Some farmers now plant wildflowers along the edges of their fields to give bees food and shelter. Even people living in apartments can help by keeping a few flowering plants on a balcony. Scientists hope that these small steps, repeated by thousands of families and farms, will slowly help bee numbers recover across the country.

qs.q: Why have bee populations dropped, according to the passage?
o: Disease, lost habitats and farm chemicals.
Flowers have stopped producing nectar in many regions.
Farmers have planted too many wildflowers near their fields.
Apple and almond trees have become too common in cities.
qs.why: 네 번째 문장이 질병, 서식지 손실, 농약을 원인으로 들어요.

qs.q: What is the purpose of the last two sentences?
o: To warn that balconies are dangerous for bees
To explain why apartments have fewer flowers
To show that ordinary people can also help bees
To ask farmers to stop growing their crops
qs.why: 마지막 두 문장은 아파트에 사는 보통 사람도 벌을 도울 수 있고, 작은 노력이 모이면 벌의 수가 회복될 수 있다는 점을 보여 줘요.

qs.q:
Where does the following sentence best fit in the passage?
"This movement of pollen is what allows plants to produce seeds and fruit."
qs.why: ‘This movement of pollen’은 바로 앞 문장(꽃가루를 옮김)을 받고, 다음 문장의 ‘Without it’이 이 과정을 가리켜요.

qs.q: Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?
o: Bees are the only animals that carry pollen anywhere.
Wildflowers grow best at the edges of apartment buildings.
Farmers no longer need to use any chemicals at all.
Fewer bees could lead to smaller harvests of some crops.
qs.why: 벌이 없으면 수확량이 줄어든다는 내용에서 추론할 수 있어요. 나머지는 글에 근거가 없어요.

items.title: Stopping Waste at the River
items.text: Every year, millions of tons of plastic waste flow from rivers into the sea. [1] Much of it breaks into tiny pieces that fish and seabirds mistake for food. [2] Cleaning the open ocean is extremely difficult because the pieces are small and spread over huge areas. [3] Some engineers have therefore started working on rivers, where waste is easier to collect before it reaches the coast. [4] To do this, floating barriers guide trash toward a collection point, and workers then sort it for recycling. Experts agree, however, that cleanup alone cannot solve the problem unless people also use less plastic in the first place. Several countries have also begun to ban single-use bags and straws, which should gradually reduce the amount of waste entering rivers.

qs.q: Why is cleaning the open ocean so difficult?
o: Fish and seabirds refuse to leave the polluted water.
Engineers cannot build barriers that float on the sea.
The waste is made of small pieces spread over wide areas.
Rivers carry more waste than the ocean can hold.
qs.why: 세 번째 문장이 조각이 작고 넓게 퍼져 있어서 어렵다고 설명해요.

qs.q: What does "it" in the fifth sentence refer to?
o: the floating barrier itself
the trash gathered at the collection point
the water in the river
the coast near the river
qs.why: 모인 쓰레기를 작업자들이 분류한다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does the writer suggest in the last two sentences?
o: Using less plastic is needed along with cleanup.
Cleanup projects should be stopped completely.
Recycling workers should sort waste out at sea.
Rivers should be closed to boats and fishers.
qs.why: 마지막 두 문장은 청소만으로는 부족하고, 플라스틱 사용 자체를 줄이는 일(일회용 봉지·빨대 금지)이 함께 필요하다고 말해요.

qs.q: According to the passage, what do experts say about cleaning up waste?
o: It works only when people also use less plastic.
It is the only step that is really needed.
It should replace all recycling work.
It is too costly to try in rivers.
qs.why: 전문가들은 정화만으로는 문제를 해결할 수 없고 플라스틱 사용도 줄여야 한다고 말해요(“cleanup alone cannot solve the problem unless people also use less plastic”).

items.title: Our First Culture Day
items.text: Last month, our school held its first Culture Day, and nearly every student took part in some way. [1] Some classes performed short plays, while others set up booths to show foods from different countries. [2] At first, the planning committee worried that few visitors would come because the event fell on a rainy Saturday. [3] Parents and neighbors filled the hallways, and the booth selling dumplings ran out of food by noon. [4] Teachers praised the students for working together, and the principal suggested making the festival an annual tradition. Next year, the committee plans to start preparing earlier and to invite students from nearby schools. Everyone agreed that the day had taught them how much a school community can achieve when each person does a small part.

qs.q:
Where does the following sentence best fit in the passage?
"The rain, however, did not keep people away, as the committee soon discovered."
qs.why: ‘however’는 앞의 우려(비 때문에 방문객이 적을 것)와 대조되고, 다음 문장이 실제로 사람이 많았다는 증거가 돼요.

qs.q: Which best describes the committee's feeling at first?
o: Concerned that the weather would reduce visitors
Excited about inviting students from other schools
Angry that many students refused to help
Bored by the number of plans to be made
qs.why: 세 번째 문장에서 비 때문에 방문객이 적을까 걱정했다고 해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the dumpling booth?
o: It opened later than the other booths did.
It was very popular with the visitors.
It was run by parents instead of students.
It sold food from only one country.
qs.why: 정오까지 음식이 다 떨어졌다는 것은 인기가 많았다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What will the committee probably do next year?
o: Prepare earlier and invite nearby schools
Ask parents to run every booth at the fair
Cancel the plays to save time for booths
Move the festival to a sunnier time of year
qs.why: 마지막 문장에 더 일찍 준비하고 이웃 학교를 초대할 계획이 나와요.

items.title: A Cup of Tea
items.text: In many parts of East Asia, drinking tea is more than a way to stay refreshed. [1] It is often a calm social ritual that gives people a reason to sit together and talk. [2] A traditional tea gathering usually begins with the host carefully warming the cups and measuring the leaves. [3] Guests, meanwhile, are expected to watch quietly, accept the cup with both hands and thank the host before drinking. [4] These small gestures show respect and help everyone slow down for a few minutes. Many young people who spend most of the day on their phones say they enjoy this peaceful break. Perhaps this is why the custom has survived for centuries, even though daily life has become faster and noisier than ever.

qs.q: What does "These small gestures" refer to?
o: Talking loudly with friends during the gathering
Checking phones between cups of tea
Accepting the cup with both hands and thanking the host
Pouring tea quickly for all of the guests
qs.why: 바로 앞 문장의 손님들의 예의 바른 행동을 가리켜요.

qs.q:
Where does the following sentence best fit in the passage?
"Every step is done slowly, so even a simple cup of tea can take half an hour to prepare and enjoy."
qs.why: ‘Every step’은 주인이 하는 여러 단계를 가리키고, 다음 문장의 ‘meanwhile’은 그 동안 손님이 하는 일을 설명해요. [4]에 넣으면 ‘These small gestures’의 지시 관계가 끊겨요.

qs.q: Why does the writer mention young people who spend most of the day on their phones?
o: To argue that phones should be banned at tea gatherings
To explain why tea sales have fallen in recent years
To show that the tradition still appeals to them
To complain that they do not have good manners
qs.why: 젊은 사람들도 이 평화로운 휴식을 즐긴다는 점을 보여 줘요.

qs.q: In the second sentence, "ritual" is closest in meaning to
o: a fixed set of customs
a sudden change of plans
a kind of cheap drink
a private argument
qs.why: ritual은 정해진 관습이나 의식을 뜻해요.

items.title: More Than Books
items.text: Public libraries were once seen mainly as quiet places to borrow printed books. Today, many of them have changed so much that some visitors never check out a single book. [1] Some branches offer free computer classes for older adults who want to learn how to send e-mail. [2] Others provide workshops where teenagers can use 3D printers and sewing machines they could not afford at home. [3] Librarians also run reading hours for toddlers, which help parents meet one another. [4] Because of these services, city officials now describe libraries as community centers rather than simple storage rooms for books. Some librarians even say that the quiet reading room is still important, but it is now only one of many spaces inside the building.

qs.q: What does "they" in the fourth sentence refer to?
o: the librarians who run the workshops
the older adults who take computer classes
the machines that are used in the workshops
the teenagers who attend the workshops
qs.why: ‘machines they could not afford’에서 they는 십 대를 가리켜요.

qs.q: In the second sentence, "check out" is closest in meaning to
o: return
borrow
donate
repair
qs.why: 책을 check out한다는 것은 빌린다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What do the reading hours for toddlers help parents do?
o: Meet one another
Borrow more books
Join computer classes
Rent study rooms
qs.why: 유아 독서 시간은 부모들이 서로 만나는 데 도움이 된다고 했어요(“which help parents meet one another”).

qs.q: How do city officials now describe libraries?
o: As places that are too costly to keep open
As centers for community life
As rooms used only for printed books
As storage spaces that should be closed
qs.why: 여섯 번째 문장에서 도서관을 지역 사회의 중심(community centers)으로 묘사한다고 해요.

items.title: Never Too Old
items.text: Many adults say they are too old to learn a new language, but research does not support this belief. It is true that young children pick up pronunciation more easily than adults do. [1] Adults, however, have advantages of their own, such as better study habits and a clearer understanding of grammar. [2] They can also set specific goals, for example learning fifty useful phrases before a trip. [3] What matters most is regular practice, not the learner's age. [4] Ten minutes every day usually brings better results than a single long lesson once a week. So instead of worrying about age, adults should choose a method they enjoy and simply keep going every single day.

qs.q: According to the passage, what is an advantage of adult learners?
o: They pronounce new words better than children.
They have more free time for long lessons.
They never forget the phrases they learn.
They can set clear goals for their study.
qs.why: 네 번째 문장이 구체적인 목표를 세울 수 있다는 장점을 말해요.

qs.q: Which study plan does the writer prefer?
o: A short lesson every day
One long lesson each week
A big review before exams
Learning fifty phrases in an hour
qs.why: 여섯 번째 문장이 매일 10분이 일주일에 한 번 하는 긴 수업보다 낫다고 해요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Children should start language lessons earlier.
Grammar is the hardest part of a new language.
Age is not the key factor in learning a language.
Travelers need to learn many new phrases.
qs.why: 글 전체가 나이보다 꾸준한 연습이 중요하다는 내용이에요.

qs.q:
Where does the following sentence best fit in the passage?
"That is why a sixty-year-old who practices daily may speak more fluently than a teenager who studies only before exams."
qs.why: ‘That is why’는 바로 앞 문장의 ‘나이가 아니라 꾸준한 연습이 중요하다’는 이유를 결과로 이어 줘요.

items.title: The Problem of Old Gadgets
items.text: Old phones, laptops and televisions are often thrown away long before they stop working. [1] Together they form electronic waste, which is growing faster than almost any other kind of household trash. [2] Both facts are good reasons to handle old devices with care rather than leaving them in a drawer or a bin. [3] Many cities now run collection points where residents can drop off broken electronics for free. [4] Workers there take the machines apart by hand, separating plastic, glass and metal for reuse. Buying a repairable phone and keeping it for a few extra years is another simple way to reduce the problem. If more manufacturers and shoppers shared this attitude, far fewer devices would end up as waste after only a short time.

qs.q:
Where does the following sentence best fit in the passage?
"Some of this waste contains valuable metals such as copper and gold, but also harmful substances such as lead."
qs.why: ‘Both facts’는 귀중한 금속과 해로운 물질이라는 두 가지 사실을 가리키므로, 그 두 사실이 나오는 문장이 [2]에 와야 해요.

qs.q: What happens at the collection points?
o: Residents repair their broken phones for free.
Machines throw away plastic, glass and metal.
Visitors buy cheaper electronics from the workers.
Workers separate materials so they can be used again.
qs.why: 다섯 번째 문장에서 작업자들이 재료를 분리해 재사용한다고 해요.

qs.q: What is the purpose of the last two sentences?
o: To praise cities for their collection points
To warn that repairable phones are rare
To suggest a way for individuals to help
To explain how to separate glass and metal
qs.why: 마지막 두 문장은 수리 가능한 휴대폰을 오래 쓰는 것처럼 개인이 할 수 있는 방법을 제안해요.

qs.q: What is the writer's main point?
o: Metals such as gold are easy to find.
Old electronics should be handled responsibly.
New devices are better than old ones.
Televisions break more often than phones.
qs.why: 글은 오래된 기기를 책임감 있게 처리해야 한다고 말해요.

items.title: Gardens in the Sky
items.text: In crowded cities, there is little ground left for gardens, so some residents have started growing plants on their roofs. [1] A rooftop garden can be as small as a few boxes of herbs or as large as a small farm. [2] As a result, the owners spend less money on air conditioning. [3] They also hold rainwater, which reduces the amount that rushes into the streets during heavy storms. [4] Of course, a roof must be strong enough to carry the weight of soil, so engineers need to check it first. Once the structure is safe, even a few vegetables can bring fresh food and a little nature to the city. Some cities even give owners a small discount on their taxes when they turn an empty roof into a green space.

qs.q: What does "They" in the fourth sentence refer to?
o: rooftop gardens
engineers
storms
streets
qs.why: ‘They also hold rainwater’의 주어는 옥상 정원이에요.

qs.q:
Where does the following sentence best fit in the passage?
"These green spaces keep buildings cooler in summer, because the plants and soil block some of the sun's heat."
qs.why: ‘As a result’의 원인이 되는 문장이 필요해요. 건물이 시원해진다는 내용이 [2]에 와야 에어컨 비용 절감으로 이어져요.

qs.q: Why do engineers need to check a roof first?
o: It has to be strong enough to hold the soil.
It must be wide enough for a small farm.
It may be too hot for plants to survive.
It should be painted before planting begins.
qs.why: 다섯 번째 문장에서 흙의 무게를 견뎌야 한다고 해요.

qs.q: Which is closest to the writer's view of rooftop gardens?
o: They are too dangerous for most cities.
They are useful if the building is safe.
They are only suitable for large farms.
They cost more than air conditioning.
qs.why: 건물이 안전하면 유용하다는 것이 글의 태도예요.

items.title: Listening in the Gallery
items.text: Visiting a museum can feel overwhelming when there are hundreds of objects and very little explanation on the walls. [1] To solve this problem, many museums now lend visitors an audio guide at the entrance. [2] Using these codes, people can choose to hear more about the paintings they love and skip the rest. [3] Some guides even offer a children's version with simple words and stories about the people who made the objects. [4] Not everyone likes wearing headphones, however, and some visitors prefer to read the printed leaflets instead. Whichever method they choose, most people agree that a little guidance makes the visit more enjoyable. A few museums also let visitors download the talks to their own phones, so that they can listen again at home.

qs.q: Why do some visitors prefer printed leaflets?
o: They find the audio talks too short.
They cannot read the codes beside objects.
They think children's guides are too simple.
They do not enjoy wearing headphones.
qs.why: 다섯 번째 문장에서 헤드폰을 쓰기 싫어하는 사람들이 있다고 해요.

qs.q: What is an advantage of the audio guide?
o: Visitors can touch the paintings freely.
Visitors can borrow guides for a week.
Visitors can skip objects they do not like.
Visitors can speak to the painters directly.
qs.why: 세 번째 문장에서 원하는 작품만 골라 들을 수 있다고 해요.

qs.q:
Where does the following sentence best fit in the passage?
"The small device plays a short talk whenever the visitor enters a number code beside an object."
qs.why: ‘these codes’는 number code를 가리키므로 코드가 소개된 문장이 audio guide 소개 문장 바로 뒤인 [2]에 와야 해요.

qs.q: What is the overall tone of the passage?
o: Sad and hopeless
Informative and balanced
Angry and critical
Playful and silly
qs.why: 오디오 가이드의 장점과 헤드폰을 싫어하는 사람들 같은 단점을 함께 차분하게 설명하는 글이에요.

items.title: Before You Climb
items.text: Every year, rescuers help hikers who started a mountain walk without preparing properly. [1] The most common mistake is wearing shoes that are designed for city streets rather than rough paths. [2] That is why experienced hikers choose boots with a firm grip long before they leave home. [3] Weather is the second concern, since conditions on a mountain can change within a single hour. [4] A light rain jacket and extra water add very little weight but can make a big difference. Finally, hikers should tell a friend their route and expected return time, in case something goes wrong. Following these simple rules does not take away the fun of the trip; it simply makes a safe return far more likely.

qs.q: What is the most common mistake mentioned in the passage?
o: Wearing shoes made for city streets
Carrying too much water on the trail
Starting the walk after dark
Leaving the route before the rain ends
qs.why: 두 번째 문장이 도시용 신발을 신는 것을 가장 흔한 실수로 들어요.

qs.q: Why does the writer say mountain weather needs attention?
o: It is always colder than in cities.
It stays the same all day long.
It only matters in the winter months.
It can change very quickly.
qs.why: 한 시간 안에도 날씨가 바뀔 수 있다고 해요.

qs.q: What is the purpose of the last sentence of the passage?
o: To explain how to choose a good rain jacket
To argue that dangerous mountains should be closed
To show that safety rules do not spoil the fun
To warn readers that most hikers never return home
qs.why: 마지막 문장은 안전 수칙이 여행의 즐거움을 해치지 않는다고 안심시켜요.

qs.q:
Where does the following sentence best fit in the passage?
"Such shoes slip easily on wet rocks, and they offer little protection for the ankles."
qs.why: ‘Such shoes’는 도시용 신발을 가리키고, 다음 문장의 ‘That is why’가 그 문제점의 결과를 말해요.

items.title: Layers of Life
items.text: Tropical rainforests cover a small part of the earth, yet they are home to an enormous number of plants and animals. [1] The tall trees form several layers, and each layer offers a different kind of food and shelter. [2] Such differences allow thousands of species to live side by side without competing for the same food. [3] Sadly, large areas of forest are cut down every year to make room for farms and roads. [4] When the trees disappear, the animals that depend on them lose their homes. Some groups now buy land to protect it, and others teach local farmers methods that need less space. Visitors who walk through a protected forest often say that the sounds of life around them are unlike anything in a city.

qs.q: Why can thousands of species live together in a rainforest?
o: They travel to other forests every year.
They use different places and different foods.
They share the same food equally.
They sleep during the hottest hours.
qs.why: 서로 다른 층의 먹이와 서식처를 쓰기 때문에 경쟁하지 않아요.

qs.q:
Where does the following sentence best fit in the passage?
"Birds and monkeys, for example, spend most of their lives in the sunny top layer, while frogs prefer the damp ground below."
qs.why: ‘for example’은 각 층이 다른 먹이와 서식처를 제공한다는 문장의 예이고, 다음 문장의 ‘Such differences’가 이 예시를 받아요.

qs.q: In the first sentence, "enormous" is closest in meaning to
o: very old
very quiet
very rare
very large
qs.why: enormous는 아주 크다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What happens to animals when trees disappear?
o: They lose the places where they live.
They move to the tallest layer.
They begin to eat farm crops.
They are taken to protected land.
qs.why: 다섯 번째 문장에서 서식처를 잃는다고 해요.

items.title: Second Life for Paper
items.text: Paper seems like a simple material, but making it from fresh trees uses a great deal of water and energy. Recycling paper, by contrast, saves much of both, as well as reducing the trash sent to landfills. [1] The process starts when used paper is collected, sorted and mixed with water to form a soft pulp. [2] Each cycle, however, makes the fibers slightly shorter, so paper can usually be recycled only a few times. [3] That is why new fibers must still be added to keep the quality high. [4] Sorting paper carefully at home, away from food waste, helps recyclers produce cleaner pulp. Small habits like these may seem unimportant, but millions of households doing them together make a clear difference.

qs.q: Why can paper not be recycled forever?
o: Ink cannot be removed from the pulp.
Recyclers run out of clean water.
Its fibers become shorter each time.
Staples stay inside the new sheets.
qs.why: 네 번째 문장에서 순환할 때마다 섬유가 짧아진다고 해요.

qs.q: What does "both" in the second sentence refer to?
o: trees and landfills
pulp and ink
paper and staples
water and energy
qs.why: 앞 문장에서 물과 에너지를 많이 쓴다고 했어요.

qs.q:
Where does the following sentence best fit in the passage?
"Ink and staples are then removed, and the clean pulp is pressed into thin new sheets."
qs.why: ‘pulp’가 처음 나온 문장 바로 뒤에 와야 하고, 다음 문장의 ‘Each cycle’이 이 재활용 과정을 가리켜요.

qs.q: What does the writer recommend to households?
o: Remove the ink from paper before disposal.
Buy only paper made from fresh trees.
Keep paper separate from food waste.
Mix all kinds of waste together in one bin.
qs.why: 여섯 번째 문장이 종이를 음식물 쓰레기와 떨어뜨려 분리하라고 해요.

items.title: The Sound of the City
items.text: Living in a big city means getting used to constant noise from traffic, building sites and crowded streets. [1] Many people say they no longer notice the sound, but there is evidence that it still affects them. [2] These effects are stronger in children, who need more sleep to grow and concentrate in class. [3] To protect residents, some cities have placed walls beside busy roads and limited night-time construction. [4] Individuals can also help, for instance by choosing quiet appliances or planting trees near their windows. Thick leaves do not block all sound, but they absorb enough to make a noticeable difference. In the long run, a quieter neighborhood is likely to be healthier as well as more pleasant to live in.

qs.q:
Where does the following sentence best fit in the passage?
"For example, loud, continuous noise can raise a person's heart rate and make it harder to fall asleep."
qs.why: ‘evidence’의 구체적 예시가 필요하고, 다음 문장의 ‘These effects’가 심박수 증가와 수면 문제를 가리켜요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about people who say they no longer notice the noise?
o: They have moved to a quiet area.
They enjoy the sound of traffic.
They sleep better than children do.
The noise may still affect them.
qs.why: 두 번째 문장에서 소리를 못 느낀다고 해도 여전히 영향을 받는다는 증거가 있다고 해요.

qs.q: What can individuals do, according to the passage?
o: Choose quiet appliances or plant trees near windows
Build walls beside the busiest roads
Limit the hours of night construction
Move away from the city center
qs.why: 다섯 번째 문장이 개인이 할 수 있는 방법을 말해요.

qs.q: In the sixth sentence, "absorb" is closest in meaning to
o: take in
send back
block completely
make louder
qs.why: 잎이 소리를 일부 흡수한다는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Rails or Runways
items.text: For short and medium trips, many travelers now prefer trains to planes. [1] One reason is convenience, because stations are usually in the middle of cities, while airports are often far away. [2] Another advantage is comfort, as seats are wider and travelers can walk around freely. [3] Trains also produce far less carbon dioxide per passenger than planes on the same route. [4] However, trains cannot cross oceans, and tickets for very long journeys can be more expensive than flights. For that reason, the best choice often depends on the distance and the budget of each traveler. Whichever they choose, travelers who compare both options in advance usually enjoy a smoother, cheaper and more relaxing trip overall.

qs.q: Which disadvantage of trains does the writer mention?
o: They are slower than ships.
They cannot travel across oceans.
They produce more carbon dioxide than planes.
Their seats are narrower than plane seats.
qs.why: 다섯 번째 문장이 바다를 건널 수 없다고 해요.

qs.q:
Where does the following sentence best fit in the passage?
"This means passengers can often step off the train and be at their destination within minutes."
qs.why: ‘This’는 역이 도시 중심에 있다는 편리함을 가리키고, 다음 문장의 ‘Another advantage’가 편리함 다음의 장점을 이어요.

qs.q: What does the best choice depend on, according to the passage?
o: the weather and the season
the size and weight of the luggage
the number of people traveling
the distance and the money available
qs.why: 여섯 번째 문장이 거리와 예산에 달려 있다고 해요.

qs.q: In the sixth sentence, "budget" is closest in meaning to
o: the time a person has to wait
the bags a person can carry
the money a person plans to spend
the places a person wants to see
qs.why: budget은 쓸 수 있는 돈의 계획을 뜻해요.

items.title: A Wall Worth Painting
items.text: A plain gray wall at the edge of a neighborhood can make the whole street feel neglected. [1] In one town, a group of art students decided to change that by painting a large mural. [2] Their ideas were combined into a single design that covered nearly forty square meters. [3] Painting took three weekends, and neighbors brought snacks, brushes and ladders to help. [4] Since the mural was finished, there has been less graffiti on the wall, and families often stop to take photographs. The students say the project taught them that art becomes more meaningful when the community takes part. Now other neighborhoods have asked the group to visit and help them turn their own empty walls into places of pride.

qs.q: What does "that" in the second sentence refer to?
o: the group of art students
the plan to take photographs
the neglected look of the street
the shortage of ladders
qs.why: ‘that’은 거리가 방치된 것처럼 보이는 상태를 가리켜요.

qs.q: What changed after the mural was finished?
o: There was less graffiti on the wall.
Neighbors began painting their own houses.
The wall was covered by tall trees.
The students moved to another town.
qs.why: 다섯 번째 문장에서 낙서가 줄었다고 해요.

qs.q:
Where does the following sentence best fit in the passage?
"Before starting, they asked residents what images they would like to see, and many people suggested local birds and old trees."
qs.why: ‘they’는 미술 학생들이고, 다음 문장의 ‘Their ideas’는 주민들이 제안한 그림을 가리켜요.

qs.q: What lesson did the students learn?
o: Large walls are easier to paint than small ones.
Neighbors should not interrupt an artist's work.
A good design needs more than three weekends.
Art is more meaningful when the community joins in.
qs.why: 마지막 본문 문장이 공동체의 참여가 의미를 더한다고 해요.

items.title: Warm Up First
items.text: Many young athletes skip the warm-up because they are in a hurry to start playing. [1] Unfortunately, cold muscles are stiff and can tear more easily when they are suddenly stretched. [2] With these changes, the muscles become softer and more flexible, so they can move through a wider range. [3] A typical routine includes five minutes of light jogging followed by gentle stretching and a few practice movements. [4] Coaches also recommend a cool-down after exercise, because slowing down gradually helps the heart return to its normal rate. Together, these habits take only ten minutes, but they can keep a player healthy for the whole season. Athletes who build such routines early in life are likely to enjoy their sport for many more years.

qs.q: Why can cold muscles be a problem?
o: They send too much blood to the heart.
They are stiff and may tear more easily.
They make a player run faster than usual.
They cause the joints to grow weaker.
qs.why: 두 번째 문장이 근육이 뻣뻣해 찢어지기 쉽다고 해요.

qs.q: What is the purpose of a cool-down?
o: To make the muscles colder before play
To help the heart slow down gradually
To prepare the legs for a faster start
To reduce the time spent on stretching
qs.why: 다섯 번째 문장이 심장이 서서히 정상으로 돌아오도록 돕는다고 해요.

qs.q: What does "these habits" in the sixth sentence refer to?
o: the hurry to begin playing
the stiffness of cold muscles
the length of the whole season
the warm-up and the cool-down
qs.why: 앞에서 설명한 준비 운동과 정리 운동을 가리켜요.

qs.q:
Where does the following sentence best fit in the passage?
"A good warm-up gently raises body temperature and sends more blood to the muscles that will be used."
qs.why: 차가운 근육의 문제 다음에 그 해결책이 오고, 다음 문장의 ‘these changes’가 체온과 혈류의 변화를 가리켜요.

items.title: Less on the Plate, Less in the Bin
items.text: In many homes, a surprising amount of food is thrown away before anyone has a chance to eat it. [1] Often the cause is simple: people buy too much at once, and some of it spoils in the refrigerator. [2] Such lists help them buy only what they need and plan meals for the whole week. [3] Restaurants and supermarkets can contribute as well, for example by selling slightly bruised fruit at a lower price. [4] Some even give unsold bread and vegetables to food banks at the end of the day. Through these steps, communities can save money, reduce pollution and make sure that good food reaches hungry people. It may take time to change old habits, but every meal that is saved is a small victory for the planet.

qs.q:
Where does the following sentence best fit in the passage?
"To avoid this, a growing number of families write a short shopping list after checking what they already have."
qs.why: ‘this’는 음식이 상하는 문제를 가리키고, 다음 문장의 ‘Such lists’가 쇼핑 목록을 받아요.

qs.q: What is one cause of food waste mentioned in the passage?
o: Buying more food than can be eaten
Cooking meals that are too spicy
Storing bread outside the refrigerator
Eating at restaurants too often
qs.why: 두 번째 문장이 한꺼번에 너무 많이 사는 것을 원인으로 들어요.

qs.q: What does "Some" in the fifth sentence refer to?
o: families with shopping lists
hungry people in the city
restaurants and supermarkets
workers at the food banks
qs.why: 앞 문장의 식당과 슈퍼마켓 중 일부를 가리켜요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: How restaurants prepare fresh bread for customers
Ways to reduce food waste at home and in business
Where food banks find volunteers to help them
Why fruit and vegetables become more expensive
qs.why: 가정과 업체가 음식물 쓰레기를 줄이는 방법이 중심이에요.

items.title: One Week Offline
items.text: Last spring, a group of high school students agreed to give up social media for one week. [1] At first, many of them felt anxious and kept reaching for their phones out of habit. [2] Freed from constant notifications, they began reading, walking with friends and talking more with their families. [3] When the week ended, most of the students chose to return, but with new limits on their daily use. [4] One student explained that she now turns off notifications during meals and homework. Their teacher said the experiment showed that small, voluntary limits work better than strict rules imposed by adults. Not every student agreed that the week was easy, but nearly everyone said they had learned something about their habits.

qs.q: How did the students feel at first?
o: Pleased to have extra free time
Proud of the new school rule
Nervous and tied to their phones
Bored by their friends' company
qs.why: 두 번째 문장에서 불안해하며 습관적으로 휴대폰을 찾았다고 해요.

qs.q:
Where does the following sentence best fit in the passage?
"By the third day, however, the urge had grown weaker, and most of them felt calmer."
qs.why: ‘however’는 처음의 불안함과 대조되고, 다음 문장의 새로운 활동은 알림에서 벗어난 뒤의 변화로 이어져요.

qs.q: What did most students do when the week ended?
o: They deleted all of their accounts.
They went back online but set limits.
They asked for another week offline.
They stopped using their phones completely.
qs.why: 네 번째 문장이 제한을 두고 돌아갔다고 해요.

qs.q: What did the teacher conclude from the experiment?
o: Limits chosen by students can work well.
Adults should ban phones in every school.
Social media is useful only at night.
One week is too short for any change.
qs.why: 여섯 번째 문장이 스스로 정한 작은 제한이 어른이 강요한 엄격한 규칙보다 효과적이라고 해요.

items.title: Predicting the Sky
items.text: Weather forecasts are much more accurate today than they were fifty years ago. [1] This improvement is mainly due to satellites that photograph clouds and measure temperatures from space. [2] These calculations are repeated many times a day as new measurements arrive. [3] Small changes in the air can grow into big differences, so long-range forecasts remain uncertain. [4] That is why meteorologists usually speak in terms of probabilities, such as a seventy percent chance of rain. A figure like that does not mean it will rain for seventy percent of the day. Understanding this helps people decide whether to carry an umbrella on a cloudy morning before school, without feeling that the forecast has failed them.

qs.q: What does "A figure like that" refer to?
o: a seventy percent chance of rain
a fifty-year improvement in accuracy
the temperatures measured from space
the number of daily calculations
qs.why: 바로 앞 문장의 확률 수치를 가리켜요.

qs.q: Why do long-range forecasts remain uncertain?
o: Satellites cannot take photographs of clouds.
Small changes in the air can grow into big differences.
Computers cannot repeat calculations quickly.
Meteorologists avoid speaking about rain.
qs.why: 네 번째 문장이 작은 변화가 큰 차이로 커지기 때문이라고 해요.

qs.q:
Where does the following sentence best fit in the passage?
"Their data is fed into powerful computers that calculate how the air will move over the next several days."
qs.why: ‘Their data’는 위성의 자료를 가리키고, 다음 문장의 ‘These calculations’가 컴퓨터의 계산을 받아요.

qs.q: What do satellites do, according to the passage?
o: They carry computers to the ground.
They produce rain over dry regions.
They calculate the chance of rain.
They photograph clouds and measure temperatures.
qs.why: 두 번째 문장이 위성의 역할을 설명해요.

items.title: The Lot on Maple Street
items.text: Behind the apartment block on Maple Street, an empty lot was once covered with weeds and broken glass. [1] Two years ago, residents asked the city for permission to turn it into a shared vegetable garden. [2] To meet that condition, they created a schedule in which each family waters and weeds on one day a week. [3] Within a year, the lot produced tomatoes, beans and peppers, and the extra vegetables were given to older neighbors. [4] The garden has also become a meeting place where people who had never spoken before now share advice and recipes. Some residents say they feel safer because the once-empty lot is now filled with people every evening. Other apartment blocks in the area are now asking how to begin similar projects of their own.

qs.q: What happens to the extra vegetables from the garden?
o: They are given to older neighbors.
They are sold at a market run by the city.
They are sent to the school cafeteria nearby.
They are kept by the families who water the plants.
qs.why: 남은 채소는 나이 든 이웃들에게 나누어 주었다고 글에 나와 있어요.

qs.q: What does "it" in the second sentence refer to?
o: the apartment block
the city office
the empty lot
the shared garden
qs.why: ‘turn it into a garden’에서 it은 빈 땅이에요.

qs.q: Why do some residents feel safer?
o: The lot is full of people in the evening.
The city has put up a tall fence.
The weeds have been cut every week.
Older neighbors guard the garden.
qs.why: 여섯 번째 문장이 저녁마다 사람들로 가득 차기 때문이라고 해요.

qs.q:
Where does the following sentence best fit in the passage?
"The city agreed, but only on the condition that the neighbors would look after the land themselves."
qs.why: ‘that condition’이 가리키는 조건이 앞 문장에 나와야 해요. 시의 허락과 조건이 [2]에 들어가야 일정표가 그 조건을 충족해요.

items.title: The Stubborn Volcano
items.text:
Dana had been looking forward to the school science fair for weeks, but on the morning of the event her model volcano refused to work, and she had only ten minutes before the judges arrived.

(A) This time the mixture foamed up and poured down the sides of the clay mountain, and the visitors clapped so loudly that Dana could not stop smiling.

(B) She had mixed the vinegar and baking soda exactly as the instructions said, yet nothing bubbled over, and a small crowd of classmates started to whisper behind her.

(C) After a moment of panic, she remembered that her baking soda had been sitting open in the cupboard for months, so she borrowed a fresh box from the teacher's desk.

qs.q: What is the most natural order of (A), (B) and (C) after the given paragraph?
qs.why: 각 문단의 첫머리 단서(연결어·시간 표현·지시어)를 따라가면 순서가 정해져요. 실패 → ‘After a moment of panic’ → ‘This time’ 성공 순으로 이어져요.

qs.q: Why did Dana's volcano fail the first time?
o: She had forgotten to add the vinegar.
Her baking soda had gone stale.
The clay mountain was too heavy.
The judges arrived ahead of schedule.
qs.why: 오랫동안 열린 채 놓여 있던 베이킹소다 때문이에요.

qs.q: Where did Dana get the fresh baking soda?
o: From a classmate's bag
From the teacher's desk
From the school cafeteria
From a shop near the school
qs.why: 교사의 책상에서 새 상자를 빌렸어요.

qs.q: How did Dana most likely feel at the end?
o: Jealous of her classmates
Embarrassed by the noise
Angry with her teacher
Delighted and relieved
qs.why: 관객의 박수를 받고 웃음을 멈추지 못했으므로 기쁘고 안도했어요.

items.title: From Seed to Shoot
items.text:
A tiny seed may look lifeless, but inside it is a small plant waiting for the right conditions. Many gardeners are surprised by how quickly the changes begin once those conditions are met in warm, damp soil. Gardeners often describe the whole process as small, quiet and almost magical to watch.

(A) Next, a thin root pushes downward to anchor the plant and to collect more water and minerals from the ground.

(B) Finally, a green shoot grows upward toward the light, and its first leaves begin to make food from sunlight.

(C) First, the seed absorbs water from the soil, which makes it swell until its hard outer coat splits open.

qs.q: What is the most natural order of (A), (B) and (C) after the given paragraph?
qs.why: 각 문단의 첫머리 단서(연결어·시간 표현·지시어)를 따라가면 순서가 정해져요. First → Next → Finally의 순서 표지어를 따라요.

qs.q: What makes the outer coat of the seed split open?
o: Heat from the sunlight above
Pressure from the growing leaves
Swelling after it takes in water
Minerals found deep in the soil
qs.why: 씨앗이 물을 흡수해 부풀기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What is the purpose of the root?
o: To push the first leaves toward the light
To protect the young seed from insects
To make food from the sunlight above
To collect water and minerals for the plant
qs.why: 뿌리는 땅에서 물과 무기질을 모아요.

qs.q: In the passage, "anchor" is closest in meaning to
o: lift up
wash away
hold in place
warm up
qs.why: anchor는 고정한다는 뜻이에요.

items.title: The Lost Map
items.text:
Minjun had moved to a new city over the summer, and on Monday morning he stood at the gate of an unfamiliar school with his heart pounding and a paper map crumpled in his hand.

(A) Just when he was about to give up, a girl noticed his map and offered to show him the way to Room 204.

(B) He walked through the corridor looking at the numbers on each door, but every classroom seemed to be full of students who already knew one another.

(C) On the way she introduced herself as Hana, and by the time they reached the room, the two of them had already agreed to eat lunch together.

qs.q: What is the most natural order of (A), (B) and (C) after the given paragraph?
qs.why: 각 문단의 첫머리 단서(연결어·시간 표현·지시어)를 따라가면 순서가 정해져요. 교실을 찾아 헤맴 → ‘Just when’ 도움을 받음 → ‘On the way’ 자기소개 순이에요.

qs.q: How did Minjun feel at the school gate?
o: Nervous about the new school
Proud of his old school
Bored by the summer holiday
Angry about his class schedule
qs.why: 심장이 뛰고 낯선 학교 앞에 서 있어서 긴장했어요.

qs.q: What had Minjun and Hana agreed to do?
o: Eat lunch together
Study in the library
Join a school club
Walk home after class
qs.why: 교실에 도착할 때쯤 점심을 같이 먹기로 했어요.

qs.q: What made the girl offer help?
o: She heard him calling for a teacher.
She saw that he was holding a map.
She had been waiting at Room 204.
She knew him from the summer.
qs.why: 그녀가 그의 지도를 보고 도움을 주었어요.

items.title: The Lost-and-Found Board
items.text:
At our school, hundreds of umbrellas, jackets and water bottles disappear every semester, and most of them are never returned to their owners, which annoys students and teachers alike. Last term, a small group of volunteers decided to look for a practical solution to the problem.

(A) To deal with this, the student council set up a lost-and-found box beside the main office and asked teachers to place any forgotten items inside.

(B) Thanks to this system, students can now check the board during lunch, and about three out of four items are claimed within a week.

(C) However, the box soon became so full that nobody could find anything, so volunteers began photographing each object and posting the pictures on a notice board.

qs.q: What is the most natural order of (A), (B) and (C) after the given paragraph?
qs.why: 각 문단의 첫머리 단서(연결어·시간 표현·지시어)를 따라가면 순서가 정해져요. 문제 해결 시도 → ‘However’ 새 문제와 개선 → ‘Thanks to this system’ 결과로 이어져요.

qs.q: Why did the volunteers begin photographing the objects?
o: The teachers wanted to sell the objects.
The council lost the first box.
The full box made items hard to find.
The students had stopped losing things.
qs.why: 상자가 가득 차서 물건을 찾기 어려웠기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What does "this system" refer to?
o: asking students to take umbrellas home
buying a bottle for each student
posting pictures of items on a notice board
locking the classrooms at lunchtime
qs.why: 사진을 찍어 게시판에 올리는 방식을 가리켜요.

qs.q: What happens to about three out of four items?
o: They are claimed within a week.
They are given to the volunteers.
They are thrown away by teachers.
They are sold to other schools.
qs.why: 마지막 문단에서 일주일 안에 주인이 찾아간다고 해요.

items.title: Speak with Confidence
items.text:
Giving a presentation in front of the class can make even confident students nervous, but a clear plan and some patient preparation make the task much easier than it first appears. Teachers often suggest following three simple stages, from the early planning to the moment you stand up and speak.

(A) On the day itself, speak slowly, look at your listeners instead of your notes, and pause briefly after each important point.

(B) Once the content is ready, practice aloud several times, preferably in front of a friend or a mirror, and time yourself.

(C) Begin by writing down the one main message you want your audience to remember, and cut anything that does not support it.

qs.q: What is the most natural order of (A), (B) and (C) after the given paragraph?
qs.why: 각 문단의 첫머리 단서(연결어·시간 표현·지시어)를 따라가면 순서가 정해져요. 준비(Begin by) → 연습(Once the content is ready) → 발표 당일(On the day itself) 순이에요.

qs.q: Why should a speaker cut some content?
o: To finish earlier than the teacher planned
To keep only what supports the main message
To hide mistakes from the audience
To avoid practicing in front of friends
qs.why: 핵심 메시지를 뒷받침하지 않는 내용은 줄이라고 해요.

qs.q: What advice is given about practice?
o: Practice silently without timing.
Practice aloud and time yourself.
Practice only the night before.
Practice only in front of the teacher.
qs.why: 두 번째 단계에서 소리 내어 연습하고 시간을 재라고 해요.

qs.q: What advice is given for the day of the talk?
o: Read the notes without stopping.
Speak as quickly as possible.
Avoid looking at the listeners.
Pause briefly after key points.
qs.why: 당일에는 중요한 부분 뒤에 잠깐 멈추라고 해요.

items.title: Water on the Move
items.text:
Water on the earth is constantly moving, although we rarely notice it. The same water that fills a puddle today may fall as rain on another continent next year, after a long journey through the air and the sea. Scientists call this endless movement a cycle, and it has three main stages that follow one another.

(A) When the drops grow too heavy to float, they fall as rain or snow, and eventually most of the water flows back to the sea.

(B) The cycle begins when the sun warms oceans and lakes, causing liquid water to turn into invisible vapor that rises into the air.

(C) High above the ground, where the air is cold, this vapor cools down and forms tiny drops that gather into clouds.

qs.q: What is the most natural order of (A), (B) and (C) after the given paragraph?
qs.why: 각 문단의 첫머리 단서(연결어·시간 표현·지시어)를 따라가면 순서가 정해져요. 증발 → ‘this vapor’ 응결 → 강수 순서예요. 두 번째 문단의 ‘this vapor’가 첫 문단을 받아요.

qs.q: What causes liquid water to turn into vapor?
o: Cold air above the clouds
Rain falling on the lakes
Warmth from the sun
Heavy drops of snow
qs.why: 태양이 바다와 호수를 데우면 증발해요.

qs.q: Why do drops fall from clouds?
o: The sun warms the clouds again.
The vapor turns into oceans.
The wind removes the cold air.
They become too heavy to float.
qs.why: 방울이 너무 무거워지면 떨어져요.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Rain falls only over the oceans.
Clouds are made of solid ice.
Water keeps moving in a continuous cycle.
Puddles never dry up in summer.
qs.why: 글 전체가 물이 끊임없이 순환한다는 내용이에요.

items.title: Learning to Float
items.text:
Seoyeon had been afraid of deep water ever since she slipped into a pool as a small child, so she always stayed in the shallow end during family holidays and watched the others swim. Her parents never forced her, but they hoped she would one day enjoy the water as much as her brother did.

(A) After a week of lessons, she dared to let go of the edge, and to her surprise, her body floated on the surface.

(B) By the end of the month, she could swim a full length of the pool, and she no longer felt the old fear.

(C) This summer, her cousin offered to teach her, and he began by letting her hold the edge of the pool while she practiced kicking.

qs.q: What is the most natural order of (A), (B) and (C) after the given paragraph?
qs.why: 각 문단의 첫머리 단서(연결어·시간 표현·지시어)를 따라가면 순서가 정해져요. ‘This summer’ → ‘After a week’ → ‘By the end of the month’의 시간 순서예요.

qs.q: What did Seoyeon's cousin let her hold while she practiced kicking?
o: A floating board from the shop
A long rope tied to a post
The edge of the pool
His arm near the deep end
qs.why: 사촌은 그녀가 수영장 가장자리를 잡고 발차기를 연습하게 했어요.

qs.q: Why was Seoyeon surprised during the lessons?
o: Her cousin stopped teaching her suddenly.
The pool became much deeper than before.
She could swim a full length without help.
Her body floated when she let go of the edge.
qs.why: 가장자리를 놓았는데 몸이 떴기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about Seoyeon at the end?
o: She will avoid deep water in future.
She has overcome her old fear.
She dislikes swimming with her cousin.
She plans to stop taking lessons.
qs.why: 더 이상 예전의 두려움을 느끼지 않는다고 해요.

items.title: Printing in Layers
items.text:
A 3D printer builds objects in a way that is very different from cutting or carving, because it creates a shape one thin layer at a time, much like stacking sheets of paper into a tall pile.

(A) The first step is to draw the object on a computer or download a ready-made design, which the software then slices into hundreds of thin layers.

(B) When the final layer is done, the object can be removed from the plate, and any rough edges are smoothed by hand.

(C) Next, the printer melts plastic thread and places it along the path of each layer, waiting for it to harden before starting the next.

qs.q: What is the most natural order of (A), (B) and (C) after the given paragraph?
qs.why: 각 문단의 첫머리 단서(연결어·시간 표현·지시어)를 따라가면 순서가 정해져요. 설계 → 인쇄 → 마무리 순이에요. ‘The first step’, ‘Next’, ‘When the final layer is done’가 단서예요.

qs.q: How does a 3D printer create a shape?
o: By carving a large block of solid plastic
By pressing hot metal into a heavy mold
By adding thin layers one on top of another
By cutting sheets of paper into small pieces
qs.why: 도입부에서 얇은 층을 하나씩 쌓아 만든다고 해요.

qs.q: What does the software do with the design?
o: It lifts the object off the plate carefully.
It cuts the design into many thin layers.
It melts the plastic thread for printing.
It removes rough edges from the finished object.
qs.why: 소프트웨어가 설계를 수백 개의 얇은 층으로 나눠요.

qs.q: What happens after the final layer is finished?
o: Rough edges are smoothed by hand.
The plastic thread is melted again.
The design is drawn on a computer.
The printer begins another layer.
qs.why: 마지막 층 뒤에 사람이 손으로 거친 부분을 다듬어요.

items.title: Grandmother's Soup
items.text:
Every winter, my grandmother makes a large pot of rice cake soup for the whole family, and every winter I promise to learn how to cook it myself, though I always seem to forget.

(A) She did not use measuring spoons, so I had to watch her hands carefully and write down words like "a little" and "until it smells right".

(B) Last weekend, I finally kept that promise by arriving at her kitchen early, with an apron on and a notebook in my hand.

(C) When we sat down to eat, the soup tasted almost like hers, and she smiled and said that my notes were the best part of the recipe.

qs.q: What is the most natural order of (A), (B) and (C) after the given paragraph?
qs.why: 각 문단의 첫머리 단서(연결어·시간 표현·지시어)를 따라가면 순서가 정해져요. ‘that promise’(첫 문단 약속) → 요리 과정 → ‘When we sat down to eat’ 순이에요.

qs.q: Why did the writer write down words like "a little"?
o: The writer could not read the recipe.
The grandmother did not measure the ingredients.
The soup needed only a little salt.
The notebook had very few pages.
qs.why: 계량스푼을 쓰지 않아서 표현을 그대로 적었어요.

qs.q: What does "that promise" in (B) refer to?
o: arriving early at the kitchen
learning to cook the soup
buying a notebook for her
inviting the whole family
qs.why: (B)의 ‘that promise’는 첫 문단에서 말한 ‘요리를 배우겠다는 약속’을 가리켜요.

qs.q: What did the grandmother's last comment show?
o: She wanted to keep the recipe secret.
She thought the soup needed more salt.
She planned to write a notebook herself.
She was pleased with the writer's careful effort.
qs.why: 노트가 가장 좋은 부분이라고 말한 것은 정성을 칭찬한 거예요.

items.title: A Day at the Shelter
items.text:
On Saturday morning, twelve students from our school volunteered at the animal shelter, where dozens of dogs and cats were waiting for new homes and a great deal of work was waiting for us. The shelter had only four full-time workers, so any extra help was warmly welcomed by everyone.

(A) At the end of the day, my dog, a shy brown puppy, finally wagged his tail when I said goodbye, and I decided to return the following week.

(B) We began by cleaning the cages, filling the water bowls and sorting donated blankets, which took almost two hours.

(C) After that, the staff showed us how to walk the dogs gently, and each of us was paired with one animal.

qs.q: What is the most natural order of (A), (B) and (C) after the given paragraph?
qs.why: 각 문단의 첫머리 단서(연결어·시간 표현·지시어)를 따라가면 순서가 정해져요. ‘We began by’ → ‘After that’ → ‘At the end of the day’의 순서예요.

qs.q: What took the students almost two hours?
o: Walking the dogs around the park
Finding new homes for the cats
Cleaning cages and sorting blankets
Saying goodbye to the puppies
qs.why: 우리를 청소하고 담요를 정리하는 데 두 시간 가까이 걸렸어요.

qs.q: In the passage, "paired with" is closest in meaning to
o: compared with
scolded by
carried by
matched with
qs.why: 각자 한 마리씩 짝지어졌다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why did the writer decide to return the next week?
o: The staff offered payment for helping.
The shelter had no other volunteers.
The puppy responded warmly at the end.
The teacher required another visit.
qs.why: 강아지가 꼬리를 흔든 일이 계기가 되었어요.

items.title: How Kimchi Is Made
items.text:
Kimchi is a traditional Korean side dish, and many families still make a large amount together in late autumn so that it will last through the cold months of winter. The work takes several days, and the whole family usually helps with each stage of the process.

(A) Then the leaves are rinsed, and a spicy paste of red pepper, garlic and ginger is spread carefully between each layer.

(B) Finally, the kimchi is packed into jars and left to ferment, developing its sour taste over the following days.

(C) First, whole cabbages are cut in half and soaked in salty water for several hours, which makes the leaves soft and draws out extra moisture.

qs.q: What is the most natural order of (A), (B) and (C) after the given paragraph?
qs.why: 각 문단의 첫머리 단서(연결어·시간 표현·지시어)를 따라가면 순서가 정해져요. First → Then → Finally의 표지어가 순서를 알려줘요.

qs.q: Why are the cabbages soaked in salty water?
o: To soften the leaves and remove moisture
To make the paste taste sweeter
To keep insects out of the jars
To turn the leaves bright red
qs.why: 소금물이 잎을 부드럽게 하고 수분을 빼 줘요.

qs.q: What is spread between the layers?
o: A paste of pepper, garlic and ginger
Slices of fresh fruit
Pieces of dry seaweed
Boiled potatoes and onions
qs.why: 두 번째 단계에서 고춧가루, 마늘, 생강 양념을 바른다고 해요.

qs.q: What happens to the kimchi in the jars?
o: It dries out and turns hard.
It ferments and becomes sour.
It is rinsed again with water.
It is cut into smaller pieces.
qs.why: 병에서 발효되며 신맛이 생겨요.

items.title: Less Homework, Same Results
items.text:
Last year, students in the second grade complained that they had so much homework that they could not sleep enough or enjoy any hobbies, and some even said they felt tired during every morning class. The principal listened carefully to their complaints and promised that the school would look for a fair solution.

(A) In response, the teachers held a meeting and agreed that each subject would assign no more than twenty minutes of homework per night.

(B) The results showed that scores had not dropped, and the students reported feeling more rested, so the rule was made permanent.

(C) At first, some parents worried that their children would learn less, so the school promised to compare test scores after one semester.

qs.q: What is the most natural order of (A), (B) and (C) after the given paragraph?
qs.why: 각 문단의 첫머리 단서(연결어·시간 표현·지시어)를 따라가면 순서가 정해져요. 대응 → ‘At first’ 우려와 약속 → 결과 순이에요.

qs.q: Why did the school compare the test scores?
o: To answer the parents' worry about learning less
To reward the students with the best marks
To find out which teacher had given the least homework
To prepare for the school festival next spring
qs.why: 학부모의 우려를 확인하려고 점수를 비교했어요.

qs.q: What was the result of the new rule?
o: Scores dropped a little, but students felt happier.
Scores rose sharply, and students had more homework.
Scores did not drop, and students felt more rested.
Parents stopped asking about the scores altogether.
qs.why: 성적은 떨어지지 않았고 학생들은 더 잘 쉬었다고 해요.

qs.q: In the passage, "permanent" is closest in meaning to
o: changed again every week
lasting for a long time
limited to a single short test
decided only by the parents
qs.why: permanent는 오래 지속되는, 영구적이라는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Starting a Band
items.text:
When Jisoo realized that her school had no music club, she decided to start a band, even though she had never organized anything before and was not sure that anyone would join her. She loved playing the guitar, and she believed that music could bring a quiet school together.

(A) The group's first practice was a disaster because everyone played a different song at the same time, but they agreed to choose one tune together.

(B) Two months later, the band performed that tune at the winter assembly, and the principal asked them to play again in the spring.

(C) She began by putting up posters in the hallway, and within a week, six students with guitars, drums and a keyboard had signed up.

qs.q: What is the most natural order of (A), (B) and (C) after the given paragraph?
qs.why: 각 문단의 첫머리 단서(연결어·시간 표현·지시어)를 따라가면 순서가 정해져요. 모집 → 첫 연습 → ‘Two months later’ 공연 순이에요.

qs.q: How did Jisoo find members for the band?
o: By asking the principal to choose
By putting up posters in the hallway
By holding a concert for parents
By visiting other schools
qs.why: 복도에 포스터를 붙였어요.

qs.q: Why was the first practice a disaster?
o: The instruments were broken.
Everyone played a different song.
Nobody came to the meeting.
The principal stopped the music.
qs.why: 모두 다른 곡을 연주했기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the winter performance?
o: It was canceled at the last minute.
It was shorter than the band expected.
It was played for the principal alone.
It was well received by the audience.
qs.why: 교장 선생님이 봄에 다시 연주해 달라고 했으므로 호평을 받았어요.

items.title: Sunscreen on a Gray Day
items.text:
Many people think sunscreen is only necessary at the beach, but dermatologists say that sunlight can damage skin even on a cloudy day, when the weather seems harmless and the sun is hard to see. Health experts therefore give several pieces of advice that are worth knowing before the summer begins.

(A) They also advise applying it again every two hours when you are outside, because sweat and water gradually wash it away.

(B) Because of these rays, doctors recommend putting sunscreen on every morning, particularly on the face, neck and hands, which are always exposed.

(C) The main reason is that ultraviolet rays pass through thin clouds, so a gray sky may still deliver most of the harmful energy.

qs.q: What is the most natural order of (A), (B) and (C) after the given paragraph?
qs.why: 각 문단의 첫머리 단서(연결어·시간 표현·지시어)를 따라가면 순서가 정해져요. 이유(C) → ‘these rays’를 받는 권고(B) → ‘They also advise’ 추가 권고(A) 순이에요.

qs.q: Why can a cloudy day still harm the skin?
o: Clouds make the air much hotter.
Sunscreen stops working in the shade.
Ultraviolet rays can pass through thin clouds.
The sun is closer on gray days.
qs.why: 얇은 구름을 자외선이 통과하기 때문이에요.

qs.q: Which parts of the body are described as always exposed?
o: The back, legs and feet
The arms, knees and ears
The hair, nose and shoulders
The face, neck and hands
qs.why: (B)에서 얼굴, 목, 손이 항상 노출된다고 말해요.

qs.q: Why should people apply sunscreen again?
o: The first layer becomes too thick.
Sunlight changes the color of the skin.
Sweat and water gradually wash it away.
Clouds move during the afternoon.
qs.why: 땀과 물이 선크림을 씻어내기 때문이에요.

items.title: The Stream Comes Back
items.text:
For years, the stream behind our village was full of bottles and plastic bags, and children were told never to go near it, since the water smelled bad and the banks were covered with sharp pieces of glass. Nobody believed that the situation could ever change, until one person decided to take action.

(A) Then a retired teacher organized a cleanup day, and nearly eighty neighbors arrived with gloves and buckets to remove the trash.

(B) Today, families walk along the path every evening, and the villagers have promised to repeat the cleanup each spring.

(C) Within a month, small fish returned to the water, and birds began to rest on the banks again.

qs.q: What is the most natural order of (A), (B) and (C) after the given paragraph?
qs.why: 각 문단의 첫머리 단서(연결어·시간 표현·지시어)를 따라가면 순서가 정해져요. 정화 활동 → ‘Within a month’ 변화 → ‘Today’ 현재 순이에요.

qs.q: What did the retired teacher do?
o: Organized a cleanup day for the neighbors
Fished in the stream every evening
Built a path along the banks
Told the children to stay away
qs.why: 정화의 날을 조직했어요.

qs.q: What is a sign that the stream had recovered?
o: Small fish and birds came back.
Children were told to avoid it.
Fewer neighbors lived nearby.
The water became warmer.
qs.why: 한 달 안에 작은 물고기와 새가 돌아왔어요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the villagers' attitude?
o: They are afraid of the stream.
They want to keep the stream clean.
They plan to move away soon.
They think the cleanup was a waste.
qs.why: 매년 봄 정화를 반복하기로 약속했어요.

items.title: The Group Report
items.text:
Jun: Our science project is due on Friday, and we still have not decided who will write the report.
[1]
Eun: I can do the writing, but I am not good at making charts, so I would need some help with the data.
[2]
Eun: Great, then I will send you my notes after dinner so that you can see which numbers I need.
[3]
Jun: Perfect. Should we also practice the presentation together, or do you prefer to prepare alone?
[4]
Eun: Together would be better, because we have to decide who speaks first and who answers the teacher's questions.
Jun: Then let us meet in the library tomorrow after class, and we can print the charts there.
Eun: Good idea. I will also bring a few pages of my draft so that we can check the order of the parts.
Jun: Sounds like a plan. If we stay organized, I think we can even finish before Friday.

qs.q:
Where does the following line best fit in the dialogue?
"That is no problem, because I enjoy working with numbers, and I can make the charts tonight."
qs.why: Eun의 어려움(차트) 바로 뒤에 Jun이 도움을 제안하고, 다음 줄의 ‘then I will send you my notes’가 그 제안에 대한 응답이에요.

qs.q: What problem does Eun mention?
o: She cannot write a long report.
She does not enjoy working with Jun.
She lost the notes for the project.
She is not good at making charts.
qs.why: Eun은 차트를 만드는 데 서툴다고 말해요.

qs.q: Why does Eun prefer to practice together?
o: They must decide who speaks and who answers questions.
They want to finish the report by Thursday evening.
Jun is afraid to speak in front of the teacher alone.
The library does not allow students to practice alone.
qs.why: 발표 순서와 질문에 답할 사람을 정해야 하기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What will they do tomorrow after class?
o: Send notes to each other by e-mail
Practice the presentation in the classroom
Meet in the library and print the charts
Ask the teacher to move the deadline
qs.why: 내일 방과 후 도서관에서 만나 차트를 인쇄해요.

items.title: A Broken Speaker
items.text:
Customer: Hello, I bought these headphones last week, but the left speaker stopped working yesterday.
[1]
Clerk: I am sorry to hear that. Do you have the receipt, and did you keep the original box?
[2]
Customer: I kept the receipt, but I threw away the box because I thought I would not need it.
[3]
Customer: Thank you. In that case, can I exchange them for the same model, or is a refund the only option?
[4]
Clerk: You can choose either one. However, a refund will take about five days to appear on your card.
Customer: Then I would prefer an exchange, because I need the headphones for an online class this evening.
Clerk: No problem. Please wait here while I bring a new pair from the storeroom and test it for you.
Customer: That is very kind of you. I really appreciate how quickly you solved the problem.

qs.q: In the dialogue, "appreciate" is closest in meaning to
o: be curious about
be afraid of
be grateful for
be worried about
qs.why: ‘appreciate’는 고마워한다는 뜻으로 ‘be grateful for’와 가까워요.

qs.q: Why does the customer choose an exchange?
o: The headphones are needed for class tonight.
The shop does not give refunds on headphones.
The card cannot receive any more payments now.
The clerk recommended a different, newer model.
qs.why: 오늘 저녁 온라인 수업에 필요하기 때문이에요.

qs.q:
Where does the following line best fit in the dialogue?
"That is fine, since our policy only requires proof of purchase and the product itself."
qs.why: 손님이 상자를 버렸다고 한 뒤에 ‘That is fine’이 오고, 다음 줄의 ‘In that case’가 이 대답을 받아 교환이나 환불을 물어요.

qs.q: What will the clerk do next?
o: Refund the money to the card
Bring a new pair and test it
Call the maker of the headphones
Check the receipt a second time
qs.why: 새 제품을 가져와 시험해 주겠다고 해요.

items.title: Chess or Drama?
items.text:
Ara: The club fair starts at three, and I still cannot decide between the chess club and the drama club.
[1]
Daniel: What do you like about each one? Maybe thinking about that will make the choice easier.
[2]
Ara: Chess helps me concentrate, but drama lets me meet more people and speak in front of an audience.
[3]
Ara: You are right, I did say that. But I am afraid I will forget my lines and embarrass myself.
[4]
Daniel: Everyone makes mistakes at first, and the teacher usually gives beginners small parts so that they can slowly gain experience.
Ara: That makes me feel better. Maybe I can try drama this semester and join the chess club next year.
Daniel: Exactly. Clubs are not permanent, so you can always change if you find that it does not suit you.
Ara: Thanks, Daniel. Let us go to the fair together, and I will sign up for drama first.

qs.q: Why does Ara like the drama club?
o: She wants to learn how to play chess.
She can meet people and speak before an audience.
Her teacher chose her for a large part.
The meetings are held before the fair.
qs.why: Ara는 사람을 만나고 청중 앞에서 말할 수 있다고 해요.

qs.q:
Where does the following line best fit in the dialogue?
"In that case, I would choose drama, since you told me last month that you wanted to become more confident on stage."
qs.why: Ara가 두 동아리의 장점을 말한 뒤에 Daniel이 ‘In that case’로 조언하고, 다음 줄의 ‘You are right, I did say that’이 그 말을 받아요.

qs.q: What is Ara worried about?
o: Losing a chess match in public
Missing the start of the fair
Choosing a club her friend dislikes
Forgetting her lines on the stage
qs.why: 대사를 잊어 창피할까 봐 걱정해요.

qs.q: What does Daniel say about clubs?
o: A student can change clubs later.
Every club accepts only beginners.
Drama is better than chess for everyone.
The fair is held twice each year.
qs.why: 동아리는 영구적이지 않아 바꿀 수 있다고 해요.

items.title: A Seaside Booking
items.text:
Agent: Good morning. How can I help you plan your trip to the coast?
[1]
Guest: My family wants to spend three nights there in July, and we would like to stay near the beach.
[2]
Agent: July is the busiest month, so I recommend booking at least two months ahead.
[3]
Agent: In that case, a family room with a kitchen may be cheaper, since you can cook some of your own meals.
[4]
Guest: That is a clever idea. Is there a supermarket within walking distance of the hotel?
Agent: Yes, there is a large one just five minutes away, and the hotel also offers a free shuttle to the beach.
Guest: Excellent. Please reserve the family room for the fourth of July, and send the details to my e-mail address.
Agent: Certainly. You will receive a confirmation message within the hour, and you can cancel for free until June.

qs.q: Why does the agent suggest a room with a kitchen?
o: It is closer to the beach than other rooms.
It is the only room left in July.
It may cost less for the family.
It has a free shuttle to the hotel.
qs.why: 직접 요리하면 더 저렴할 수 있기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What does the guest ask about?
o: A restaurant on the beach
A bus to the airport
A swimming pool for children
A supermarket near the hotel
qs.why: 호텔 가까이에 슈퍼마켓이 있는지 물어요.

qs.q: What can the guest do until June?
o: Change the room for a larger one
Book a trip for the next summer
Cancel the booking without paying
Receive a gift from the hotel
qs.why: 6월까지는 무료로 취소할 수 있다고 해요.

qs.q:
Where does the following line best fit in the dialogue?
"Two months ahead is no problem, but we are worried about the price because we have two children."
qs.why: 손님이 가격 걱정을 말한 뒤에 직원이 ‘In that case’로 더 저렴한 방을 권해요.

items.title: The Missed Shot
items.text:
Coach: Jiho, you looked unhappy at the end of the match. Is something bothering you?
[1]
Jiho: I missed the last shot, and we lost by one point. I feel as if I let the whole team down.
[2]
Jiho: I suppose that is true, but I keep seeing the ball bounce off the ring in my head.
[3]
Coach: Every player remembers a missed shot. What matters is how you prepare for the next game.
[4]
Jiho: Should I practice free throws after class? I have an hour free every day before dinner.
Coach: That is a good plan, but also rest enough, because tired players make more mistakes than rested ones.
Jiho: I will do both. Thank you, Coach, for not blaming me in front of the others.
Coach: A team wins and loses together, and I am proud of the effort you gave today.

qs.q:
Where does the following line best fit in the dialogue?
"One shot never decides a game, and you scored eleven points before that."
qs.why: Jiho의 자책 뒤에 코치가 위로하고, 다음 줄의 ‘that is true’가 그 위로를 받아요.

qs.q: How does Jiho feel at first?
o: Proud of scoring eleven points
Guilty about losing the match
Angry with the other players
Excited about the next game
qs.why: 마지막 슛을 놓쳐 팀을 실망시켰다고 느껴요.

qs.q: What does the coach mean by "A team wins and loses together"?
o: No single player is to blame.
Every player must score the same points.
The coach decides who wins each game.
Practice is not needed after a loss.
qs.why: 승패는 팀 전체의 몫이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What will Jiho probably do?
o: Practice free throws and also rest enough
Quit the team before the next game
Practice every night until very late
Ask the coach for a different position
qs.why: 자유투 연습을 하고 충분히 쉬겠다고 해요.

items.title: Rain on Saturday
items.text:
Sora: Have you checked the forecast for Saturday? I am worried about our hiking trip.
[1]
Minho: Yes, I did. It says there will be heavy rain in the morning, with strong wind in the afternoon.
[2]
Sora: That is disappointing. We booked the bus tickets two weeks ago, and I was really looking forward to it.
[3]
Sora: That would work for me, but the bus tickets are only valid for Saturday.
[4]
Minho: Then let us call the bus company tomorrow morning and ask whether we can change the date.
Sora: Good idea. If they refuse, we can still use the tickets for a shorter trip next month.
Minho: Right. In the meantime, I will pack the food so that we can leave early on Sunday.
Sora: Thanks. I will bring the maps and check the trail again tonight.

qs.q: What problem does Sora mention about the bus tickets?
o: They were bought for the wrong destination.
They are too expensive to change.
They have already been used once.
They are valid only for Saturday.
qs.why: 버스표가 토요일에만 유효하다고 해요.

qs.q:
Where does the following line best fit in the dialogue?
"We could go on Sunday instead, because the forecast says the weather will be clear all day."
qs.why: Sora의 실망 뒤에 Minho가 일요일을 제안하고, 다음 줄의 ‘That would work for me’가 그 제안을 받아요.

qs.q: What do they plan to do tomorrow morning?
o: Buy new tickets for Sunday morning
Call the bus company about the date
Bring the food to the bus station
Check the trail again with a map
qs.why: 내일 아침 버스 회사에 전화해 날짜 변경을 물을 거예요.

qs.q: What will Minho do to prepare?
o: Bring the maps for the trail
Pay for the tickets again
Pack the food for the hike
Cancel the trip completely
qs.why: 일찍 출발하도록 음식을 챙기겠다고 해요.

items.q:
Choose the most natural order of the sentences.
Mina wanted to bake bread for her family.
(A) Then she covered the dough with a cloth and left it to rise for an hour.
(B) Finally, she baked it in a hot oven until the crust turned golden brown.
(C) She started by mixing flour, water and yeast in a large bowl.
items.why: 연결어와 지시어, 시간 표현을 단서로 순서를 정해요. ‘started by’ → ‘Then’ → ‘Finally’ 순서예요.

items.q:
Choose the most natural order of the sentences.
Our school library recently introduced a new rule about borrowing books.
(A) To prevent this, every book must now be returned within two weeks, so more readers can enjoy it.
(B) Previously, students could keep a book for as long as they wished.
(C) As a result, popular titles often disappeared from the shelves for months.
items.why: 연결어와 지시어, 시간 표현을 단서로 순서를 정해요. 과거의 상황(Previously) → 결과(As a result) → 문제를 막기 위한 새 규칙(To prevent this) 순서예요.

items.q:
Choose the most natural order of the sentences.
A small village was suffering from a long dry season.
(A) In response, the villagers dug a channel to bring water from a distant river.
(B) The wells slowly ran empty, and farmers could no longer water their fields.
(C) Soon the green crops returned, and the village was no longer short of water.
items.why: 연결어와 지시어, 시간 표현을 단서로 순서를 정해요. 문제 → ‘In response’ 해결 → ‘Soon’ 결과 순서예요.

items.q:
Choose the most natural order of the sentences.
Choosing a good password is important for keeping your accounts safe.
(A) Once you have a strong password, do not share it with anyone, even close friends.
(B) Instead, combine several unrelated words with numbers and symbols.
(C) First, avoid using obvious information such as your birthday or your name.
items.why: 연결어와 지시어, 시간 표현을 단서로 순서를 정해요. ‘First’ → ‘Instead’ → ‘Once you have’ 순서예요.

items.q:
Choose the most natural order of the sentences.
Hana was nervous about her first violin concert.
(A) On the evening of the concert, her hands trembled as she walked onto the stage.
(B) When the last note ended, the audience stood and clapped for a long time.
(C) However, once the first notes filled the hall, her fear slowly disappeared.
items.why: 연결어와 지시어, 시간 표현을 단서로 순서를 정해요. 무대에 오름 → ‘However’ 두려움이 사라짐 → 연주 끝 순서예요.

items.q:
Choose the most natural order of the sentences.
The Moon appears to change shape during the month.
(A) The change we see depends on how much of the lit half faces the earth.
(B) That is why it looks like a thin curve on some nights and a full circle on others.
(C) In reality, it is always round, and half of it is always lit by the sun.
items.why: 연결어와 지시어, 시간 표현을 단서로 순서를 정해요. 사실 → 원인 → ‘That is why’ 결과 순서예요.

items.q:
Choose the most natural order of the sentences.
Many people believe that a balanced breakfast helps students focus.
(A) For this reason, even a simple breakfast of fruit and yogurt is better than nothing.
(B) To begin with, food gives the brain the energy it needs after a night without eating.
(C) Students who skip it often feel tired and find it hard to concentrate in morning classes.
items.why: 연결어와 지시어, 시간 표현을 단서로 순서를 정해요. ‘To begin with’ → 아침을 거르면 → ‘For this reason’ 순서예요.

items.q:
Choose the most natural order of the sentences.
Last year, a town decided to replace its old streetlights.
(A) Therefore, the council installed new lamps that give the same light with much less power.
(B) A year later, the town had saved enough money to repair its public pool.
(C) The old lamps used a lot of electricity, and the town paid high bills every month.
items.why: 연결어와 지시어, 시간 표현을 단서로 순서를 정해요. 문제 → ‘Therefore’ → ‘A year later’ 순서예요.

items.q:
Choose the most natural order of the sentences.
Leo's phone stopped working just before an important call.
(A) He first checked whether the battery was empty, but it still showed half power.
(B) Relieved, he made the call and promised himself to update the phone that weekend.
(C) Next, he restarted the device, and the screen finally came back to life.
items.why: 연결어와 지시어, 시간 표현을 단서로 순서를 정해요. ‘first’ → ‘Next’ → ‘Relieved’ 순서예요.

items.q:
Choose the most natural order of the sentences.
Traveling abroad requires some paperwork.
(A) Only when both documents are ready should you pay for the tickets and the hotel.
(B) After that, check whether the country you plan to visit requires a visa.
(C) Before booking a flight, make sure your passport will not expire within six months.
items.why: 연결어와 지시어, 시간 표현을 단서로 순서를 정해요. 여권 → ‘After that’ 비자 → ‘both documents’ 순서예요.

items.q:
Choose the most natural order of the sentences.
A museum guide explained how ancient people stored food.
(A) In cold regions, by contrast, they simply buried food in ice or snow.
(B) In warm regions, they dried fruit and meat in the sun to keep it from rotting.
(C) Both methods worked because bacteria grow slowly when there is little water or heat.
items.why: 연결어와 지시어, 시간 표현을 단서로 순서를 정해요. ‘by contrast’는 앞의 따뜻한 지역 방법과 대조되고, ‘Both methods’는 두 방법을 모두 말한 뒤에 와요.

items.q:
Choose the most natural order of the sentences.
Ji-ho wanted to raise money for a local animal shelter.
(A) He started by asking his classmates to donate books they no longer needed.
(B) In the end, he handed over the money, and the shelter bought food and blankets with it.
(C) Next, he sold the books at a stall in front of the school on Saturday.
items.why: 연결어와 지시어, 시간 표현을 단서로 순서를 정해요. 모금 시작 → ‘Next’ 판매 → ‘In the end’ 전달 순서예요.

items.q:
Where does the given sentence best fit?
Given: "This trapped air acts as a barrier, so the heat from your body stays close to you."
Sleeping bags are designed to keep campers warm at night. [1] The outer layer is usually made of nylon, which blocks wind and light rain. [2] The inside is filled with soft material that traps air. [3] That is why a thicker bag, which traps more air, feels warmer. [4] Choose a bag that matches the lowest temperature you expect.
items.why: ‘This trapped air’는 세 번째 문장의 ‘traps air’를 가리켜요.

items.q:
Where does the given sentence best fit?
Given: "However, his coach encouraged him to practice a little every morning."
Marco joined the swimming team in September. [1] At first, he could barely finish one lap without stopping. [2] After three months of this routine, he could swim ten laps in a row. [3] Now he dreams of competing in the regional championship. [4] His coach says that patience was the key.
items.why: ‘However’는 처음의 어려움과 대조되고, 다음 문장의 ‘this routine’이 매일 아침 연습을 가리켜요.

items.q:
