Where does the given sentence best fit?
Given: "Bacteria need moisture to grow, so they cannot survive in such a dry environment."
Honey never seems to spoil, even after many years in a cupboard. [1] This is partly because it contains very little water. [2] In addition, honey is slightly acidic, which makes it harder for germs to live. [3] As a result, a jar stored properly can stay good for a very long time. [4] Still, it should be kept tightly closed so that it does not absorb moisture from the air.
items.why: ‘such a dry environment’는 물이 거의 없다는 앞 문장을 받고, 다음의 ‘In addition’이 또 다른 이유를 더해요.

items.q:
Where does the given sentence best fit?
Given: "Despite these advantages, there are some risks that buyers should keep in mind."
Online shopping has become popular in the last decade. [1] Customers can compare prices from home and receive goods at their door. [2] For instance, photos on a website may not show the true color of a product. [3] Reading reviews before buying can reduce such disappointment. [4] Sensible shoppers also check the return policy in advance.
items.why: ‘these advantages’는 앞 문장의 장점을 가리키고, 다음 문장의 ‘For instance’가 위험의 예를 들어요.

items.q:
Where does the given sentence best fit?
Given: "However, most of them are too hot or too cold for living things."
Scientists have discovered thousands of planets outside our solar system. [1] Only a few lie in the habitable zone, where liquid water could exist. [2] Those few are now the main targets for future telescopes. [3] Finding even one with water would be a major discovery. [4] Until then, researchers will keep improving their instruments.
items.why: ‘However’와 ‘most of them’이 첫 문장의 행성들을 받고, 다음 문장의 ‘Only a few’와 이어져요.

items.q:
Where does the given sentence best fit?
Given: "This sorting made the next step easier, since volunteers could quickly find what each family needed."
Last year, our class collected old clothes for a charity drive. [1] Each student brought at least three items from home. [2] By the end of the week, the pile almost reached the ceiling. [3] The teacher then asked everyone to sort the clothes by size. [4] On Saturday, the volunteers handed the clothes to families in need.
items.why: ‘This sorting’은 바로 앞 문장의 분류 작업을 가리켜요.

items.q:
Where does the given sentence best fit?
Given: "City officials answer that the benefits justify the expense, because more residents can look for jobs online."
Many cities now offer free Wi-Fi in public parks. [1] Residents can use it to read the news, study or video-call relatives. [2] Critics, however, worry about the cost of keeping the network running. [3] In their view, public Wi-Fi is as basic as lighting in the streets. [4] The debate is likely to continue as more people depend on the internet.
items.why: ‘the expense’는 앞의 비용 우려를 받고, 다음의 ‘In their view’는 시 공무원들의 입장을 이어요.

items.q:
Where does the given sentence best fit?
Given: "A few simple habits can reduce this anxiety considerably."
Many students feel anxious before a big exam. [1] First, make a realistic study plan several weeks in advance. [2] Second, take short breaks so that your mind does not become tired. [3] Finally, sleep well the night before. [4] Together, these habits turn a stressful week into a manageable one.
items.why: ‘this anxiety’는 첫 문장을 가리키고, 뒤에 First, Second, Finally로 습관이 이어져요.

items.q:
Where does the given sentence best fit?
Given: "Because customers with and without allergies ordered it, the baker now prepares twice as many loaves each morning."
A bakery in our neighborhood recently introduced a new bread. [1] It is made with local rice flour instead of wheat. [2] Customers who are allergic to wheat were delighted. [3] Others simply liked its soft, slightly sweet taste. [4] Still, the loaves are usually sold out by noon.
items.why: ‘with and without allergies’는 두 부류의 손님이 모두 나온 뒤에 가능하고, 다음의 ‘Still’이 결과를 이어요.

items.q:
Where does the given sentence best fit?
Given: "This process, known as bleaching, leaves the reef empty and gray."
Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor. [1] Yet they support a quarter of all marine species. [2] Rising sea temperatures cause corals to lose their color and sometimes die. [3] Fish that depend on the reef for shelter must then move away or starve. [4] Reducing carbon emissions is one way to give reefs a chance to recover.
items.why: ‘This process’는 산호가 색을 잃는 현상을 가리키고, 다음 문장의 ‘then’이 그 결과를 이어요.

items.q:
Where does the given sentence best fit?
Given: "Last spring, however, a group of retired engineers offered to repair it for free."
The town's old clock tower had stood silent for decades. [1] They spent weeks studying the original plans and searching for matching parts. [2] On the day of the ceremony, the bells rang for the first time in forty years. [3] Many residents wept as they listened. [4] The mayor promised to keep the tower in perfect condition.
items.why: 다음 문장의 ‘They’가 가리키는 대상(기술자들)이 먼저 나와야 해요.

items.q:
Where does the given sentence best fit?
Given: "For that reason, scientists try to protect the oldest members of each herd."
Elephants are known for their remarkable memories. [1] A herd's leader, usually an old female, remembers where water can be found during droughts. [2] Young elephants watch her carefully and learn the routes. [3] When the leader dies, this knowledge may be lost. [4] Their experience is a kind of library that the whole group depends on.
items.why: ‘For that reason’은 지식이 사라질 수 있다는 앞 문장의 이유를 받고, 다음 문장의 ‘Their experience’가 가장 나이 든 구성원을 가리켜요.

items.q:
Which sentence is the most natural continuation of the paragraph?
Tom had studied hard for the driving test, but on the day of the exam he felt his hands shaking. He took a deep breath and tried to remember his instructor's advice.
o: Slowly, the shaking stopped, and he started the engine with a calmer mind.
Tom's favorite food has always been spicy noodles with lots of vegetables.
He was completely calm and had never felt nervous at any time in his life.
Six months later, he had already driven across the whole country alone.
items.why: 깊게 숨을 쉰 뒤의 자연스러운 다음 상황은 침착해져 시험을 시작하는 것이에요. 나머지는 화제 이탈, 앞 내용과 모순, 성급한 비약이에요.

items.q:
Which sentence is the most natural continuation of the paragraph?
Public transport in the city is becoming more crowded every year. Many commuters now spend more than an hour on buses and trains each day.
o: Cats are popular pets because they need less attention than dogs do.
To solve this problem, the city plans to add new lines and run trains more often.
Commuters actually enjoy long journeys much more than very short ones.
Next year, every commuter will travel for free and no one will ever complain.
items.why: 문제 상황 다음에는 해결책이 이어지는 것이 자연스러워요.

items.q:
Which sentence is the most natural continuation of the paragraph?
The first step in writing an essay is choosing a topic that interests you. A topic you enjoy will make the research and the writing much easier.
o: Famous authors often write their best essays at midnight in silent rooms.
However, a topic you dislike usually makes the essay easier to write well.
After you finish the final draft, you should hand it in to the teacher.
Once you have chosen, make a short outline listing your main points in order.
items.why: 주제를 고른 다음 단계는 개요 작성이에요. 나머지는 화제 이탈, 모순, 단계 건너뛰기예요.

items.q:
Which sentence is the most natural continuation of the paragraph?
Sofia lost her house key on the way home from school. She searched her bag twice, but it was nowhere to be found.
o: Her school bag was made of strong blue cloth that never tears or fades.
She found the key at once and walked straight into the house alone.
Finally, she called her mother, who opened the door with the spare key.
The next morning, she received a prize for never losing anything at all.
items.why: 열쇠를 못 찾은 상황에서 해결 행동이 이어지는 것이 자연스러워요.

items.q:
Which sentence is the most natural continuation of the paragraph?
Bamboo grows faster than most other plants, and some kinds can grow almost a meter in a single day. Because of this speed, bamboo is considered an excellent renewable material.
o: Bamboo grows slowly, so builders avoid it for most of their projects.
Many people enjoy hiking in the mountains during the cool autumn months.
Builders use it for floors, furniture and even scaffolding on tall construction sites.
A meter is equal to one hundred centimeters in the metric system.
items.why: 재생 가능한 재료라는 평가 다음에는 쓰임새가 이어져요.

items.q:
Which sentence is the most natural continuation of the paragraph?
Ms. Lee asked the class to describe their favorite place. Most students chose beaches or amusement parks, but Jin wrote about the old bookstore near his house.
o: He explained that its quiet corners and the smell of paper made him feel at home.
Beaches are usually crowded in July and August, so some tickets are expensive.
Therefore, the teacher decided to cancel the lesson about favorite places.
Jin has never been inside the bookstore that he wrote about in his essay.
items.why: 서점을 선택한 진의 이유를 설명하는 문장이 자연스러워요.

items.q:
Which sentence is the most natural continuation of the paragraph?
During the storm, the power in our neighborhood went out for six hours. We lit candles and gathered in the living room because the house was getting cold.
o: Electric cars have become cheaper and more popular in many countries.
Because the lights were so bright, nobody could see the candles clearly.
The electricity company announced that it will build a new power station.
To pass the time, my father told stories while my sister played quiet games.
items.why: 정전 중 가족이 시간을 보내는 모습이 자연스럽게 이어져요.

items.q:
Which sentence is the most natural continuation of the paragraph?
Many fruits turn brown after they are cut. This happens because a substance inside the fruit reacts with oxygen in the air.
o: Oxygen is the gas that all living animals need in order to breathe.
Adding a few drops of lemon juice slows this reaction, so the slices stay fresh longer.
Because of this, fruits should always be cut with the largest knife available.
Brown fruit is never safe to eat, and it can never be recycled in any way.
items.why: 원인 설명 다음에는 이를 늦추는 방법이 이어지는 것이 자연스러워요.

items.q:
Choose the best word for the blank.
The restaurant was famous for its seafood. ____, many tourists waited more than an hour for a table.
o: Nevertheless
Consequently
Otherwise
In contrast
items.why: 유명하다는 것이 원인이고 오래 기다린 것은 결과예요.

items.q:
Choose the best word for the blank.
She had never played the piano before. ____, she learned a simple song in one week.
o: Consequently
Likewise
For instance
Nevertheless
items.why: 경험이 없었다는 내용과 대조되는 결과이므로 양보의 연결어가 알맞아요.

items.q:
Read the sentences.
"The city built a new bridge and widened two roads. These projects reduced travel time by twenty percent."
What does "These projects" refer to?
o: building the bridge and widening the roads
twenty percent of the travel time
the cities near the new bridge
reducing the time spent on trips
items.why: 지시어 ‘These projects’는 앞 문장의 다리 건설과 도로 확장을 가리켜요.

items.q:
Choose the best word for the blank.
The first plan was cheap and quick. ____, it ignored the needs of older residents.
o: Therefore
Similarly
However
As a result
items.why: 장점을 말한 뒤 단점을 소개하므로 대조의 however가 알맞아요.

items.q:
Choose the best word for the blank.
Some cities have banned cars from their centers, ____ others have simply raised parking fees.
o: because
unless
so that
whereas
items.why: 두 도시의 서로 다른 접근을 대비하므로 whereas가 알맞아요.

items.q:
Choose the best word for the blank.
Hana rarely eats snacks; ____, she keeps a bag of nuts in her desk for emergencies.
o: therefore
likewise
nevertheless
furthermore
items.why: 간식을 거의 먹지 않지만 비상용으로 두는 것은 대조예요.

items.q:
Choose the best word for the blank.
____ the project ended in failure, the team learned a great deal from it.
o: Unless
Although
Whenever
So that
items.why: 실패했지만 많이 배웠다는 양보 관계이므로 Although가 알맞아요.

items.q:
Read the sentences.
"Many farmers plant trees beside their fields. Such trees protect crops from strong wind."
What does "Such trees" refer to?
o: trees planted beside the fields
trees that grow in the forest
trees that farmers cut down
trees that give sweet fruit
items.why: ‘Such trees’는 밭 옆에 심은 나무를 가리켜요.

items.good: Had I known about the traffic, I would have left earlier.
items.ko: 교통 상황을 알았더라면 더 일찍 출발했을 텐데.
bad: Had I known about the traffic, I will have left earlier.
If I had knew about the traffic, I would have left earlier.
Had I knew about the traffic, I would have left earlier.

cz.st: ___ I known about the traffic, I would have left earlier.

items.rule: 가정법 과거완료의 if를 생략하면 Had + 주어 + 과거분사 순으로 도치돼요. 주절은 would have + 과거분사예요.
items.hint: if 없이 조건을 나타내는 도치 구문이에요.

items.good: Not only did she finish the report, but she also checked every figure.
items.ko: 그녀는 보고서를 끝냈을 뿐만 아니라 모든 수치도 확인했다.
bad: Not only she finished the report, but she also checked every figure.
Not only did she finished the report, but she also checked every figure.
Not only does she finish the report, but she also checked every figure.

cz.st: Not only ___ she finish the report, but she also checked every figure.

items.rule: Not only가 문장 앞에 오면 조동사가 주어 앞으로 도치되고 동사는 원형을 써요. 뒤 절의 시제(과거)와 맞춰야 해요.

items.good: The report, which was written by Mia, won first prize.
bad: The report, that was written by Mia, won first prize.
The report, which written by Mia, won first prize.
The report, who was written by Mia, won first prize.

cz.st: The report, ___ was written by Mia, won first prize.

items.rule: 쉼표로 덧붙이는 계속적 용법의 관계대명사로는 that을 쓸 수 없고, 사물이면 which를 써요.

items.good: Having finished the exam, the students left the room quietly.
items.ko: 시험을 마치고 학생들은 조용히 교실을 나갔다.
bad: Having finish the exam, the students left the room quietly.
Having finished the exam, the room was left quietly by the students.
Having been finished the exam, the students left the room quietly.

cz.st: ___ the exam, the students left the room quietly.

items.rule: 먼저 일어난 일은 완료 분사구문 Having + 과거분사로 나타내요. 분사구문의 의미상 주어는 주절의 주어와 같아야 해요.
items.hint: 시험을 마친 것이 교실을 나간 것보다 먼저예요.

items.good: It was the lack of sleep that made him so careless.
items.ko: 그를 그렇게 부주의하게 만든 것은 수면 부족이었다.
bad: It was the lack of sleep what made him so careless.
It was the lack of sleep who made him so careless.
It were the lack of sleep that made him so careless.

cz.st: It was the lack of sleep ___ made him so careless.

items.rule: It is/was ... that 강조 구문에서는 강조되는 말이 사물이면 that을 써요. who는 사람, what은 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: No sooner had we sat down than the rain began to fall.
bad: No sooner we had sat down than the rain began to fall.
No sooner had we sat down as the rain began to fall.
No sooner had we sat down that the rain began to fall.

cz.st: No sooner had we sat down ___ the rain began to fall.

items.rule: No sooner + had + 주어 + 과거분사 + than ... 구문이에요. 부정어구가 앞에 오므로 도치되고, 짝은 than이에요.

items.good: The more you practice, the more confident you become.
bad: The more you practice, the most confident you become.
More you practice, the more confident you become.
The more you practice, more confident you become.

cz.st: The more you practice, ___ more confident you become.

items.rule: ‘the + 비교급, the + 비교급’은 ‘~할수록 더 …하다’를 뜻해요. 두 절 모두 the가 필요해요.
items.hint: 두 절의 형태가 짝을 이루는 구문이에요.

items.good: Despite the heavy rain, the match went ahead as planned.
bad: Despite of the heavy rain, the match went ahead as planned.
Despite the rain was heavy, the match went ahead as planned.
Despite the heavy rain, the match went ahead as plans.

cz.st: ___ the heavy rain, the match went ahead as planned.

items.rule: despite는 뒤에 of 없이 명사(구)가 와요. 절을 이끌려면 although를 쓰고, 의미상 ‘~ 때문에’인 because of는 맞지 않아요.

items.good: By the time we arrived, the film had already started.
items.ko: 우리가 도착했을 때 영화는 이미 시작되어 있었다.
bad: By the time we arrive, the film had already started.
By the time we had arrived, the film already starts.
By the time we arrived, the film has already started.

cz.st: By the time we arrived, the film ___ already started.

items.rule: 도착한 시점(과거)보다 먼저 시작된 일은 과거완료(had + 과거분사)로 나타내요.

items.good: Neither the teacher nor the students were aware of the change.
items.ko: 선생님도 학생들도 그 변경을 알지 못했다.
bad: Neither the teacher nor the students was aware of the change.
Neither the teacher or the students were aware of the change.
Neither the teacher nor the students is aware of the change.

cz.st: Neither the teacher nor the students ___ aware of the change.

items.rule: neither A nor B에서 동사는 가까운 B(the students)에 일치시켜요. neither의 짝은 nor예요.

items.good: Rarely do people notice how much energy a phone charger uses.
items.ko: 사람들은 휴대폰 충전기가 얼마나 많은 에너지를 쓰는지 좀처럼 알아채지 못한다.
bad: Rarely people do notice how much energy a phone charger uses.
Rarely do people to notice how much energy a phone charger uses.
Rarely people notice how much energy a phone charger uses.

cz.st: Rarely ___ people notice how much energy a phone charger uses.

items.rule: rarely 같은 부정 부사가 문두에 오면 조동사가 주어 앞으로 가는 도치가 일어나요.
items.hint: 빈도 부사가 문장 맨 앞에 있어요.
